notes: Assertions are added in the QA phase. Many are graded programmatically by running scripts/clean_check.py on the produced Python and asserting it is clean / cleaner than baseline.

evals.name: refactor-messy-order-service
evals.prompt: Review and refactor this Python class for clean-code problems. Return the improved version and a short list of what you changed and why. File: evals/fixtures/messy_order_service.py
evals.expected_output: Refactored class: PascalCase class name, type hints throughout, no mutable default argument, encapsulated state (no leaking self.items by reference, copies/immutable view), predicate named is_/has_, specific exception handling (no bare except / except-pass / print), monetary math not floating mutation, single clear responsibility. clean_check should report far fewer findings than the original.

evals.name: build-salesitem-rest-endpoint
evals.prompt: Write a small, production-quality Python module for a 'sales item' REST API with create and get-by-id operations. Include a repository abstraction with one concrete in-memory implementation, request/response models separate from the persistence entity, and proper error handling for not-found. Use FastAPI-style or framework-agnostic controllers, your call. Make it idiomatic and type-safe.
evals.expected_output: Repository defined as an interface/Protocol with a concrete impl (program-against-interfaces). DTOs separate from entity. Not-found raised as a domain error and mapped to 404. Full type hints. No leaked mutable state. clean_check clean.

evals.name: review-risky-function
evals.expected_output: Flags: mutable default arg (cache={}), bare except, SQL injection via string concatenation (parameterize), shadowing builtin id, missing type hints, silent cache of failures. Provides a corrected version with parameterized query, no mutable default, specific exception, type hints.

evals.name: exception-handling-architecture
evals.prompt: I'm writing a Python microservice with controller, service, and repository layers. How should I design exception/error handling across these layers so the API returns clean responses without leaking internals? Show the key Python pieces.
evals.expected_output: Domain-specific exception hierarchy (base ServiceError + EntityNotFoundError etc.), repository raises domain errors, service lets them propagate or wraps infra errors, controller maps exceptions to HTTP status + safe message, no stack traces leaked in production, logging at the boundary. Type-hinted example code.

evals.name: write-tests-for-pricing
evals.expected_output: Clear test names describing behavior, arrange-act-assert, boundary cases (0, 100, negative, >100 raises), parametrization for the happy path, uses pytest.raises for the error case. clean_check clean.
